These are interesting ideas. I'm not following all the details yet. Although I have tested bitcoin and use a password manager I'm not familiar enough with bitcoin wallets to understand the Zero Knowledge signin mechanism.

Really no one is doing it in bitcoin, even though they should, so it's not really a bitcoin thing. It's more of a general cryptography thing.

Basically if you have a public and private key you can sign a message. It works just like a regular signature in real life and it just say you are you.

Bitcoin addresses just happen to be based on public and private key pairs and already have established guis. People have for a long time talked about moving away from passwords because they are a really poor security feature. I figured the path of least resistance to moving beyond passwords would be this way.

If it takes off so many other things will get a lot more secure. Most credit card theft comes from the fact that your number (your identifier) is also an authorizer. You can think of it as signing in with just your username. Then there is the code on the back that you could think of as a password for more secure transactions. It's three digits with only numbers... A system like this is really needed in the financial world but it can only take off if it's convenient, and that means people need to be used to doing it.
